items.title: Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France
items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron gives a national address after widespread disorder and as some looting continued in Paris.

items.title: What we know so far about deadly fire at Canadian military base
items.summary: At least four people are confirmed to have died after a huge fire swept through the base.

items.title: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion
items.summary: The Green Party leader said, while he wanted to amend it, the motion would stand until 2028.

items.title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis
items.summary: BBC News hears from users, dealers, prison and recovery workers as the country battles with a deadly new drug epidemic.

items.title: Inside Chicago's battle against the synthetic drugs flooding the US
items.summary: A new wave of synthetic drugs is sweeping across the United States, raising fear of a worsening drug crisis. The BBC's Quentin Sommerville reports from the frontlines in South Side, Chicago, where communities are battling the crisis.

items.title: Cindy Crawford 'beyond heartbroken' after death of son Presley at 27
items.summary: Presley Gerber's death in September is being investigated as a suspected overdose.

items.title: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
items.summary: At least one person was killed in the strikes, which also hit a data centre used by Russia's equivalent of Facebook.

items.title: Ending corridor care in hospitals for children a priority, says health secretary
items.summary: Yvette Cooper also announces £140m investment in England's urgent care system, ahead of winter.
